title: Model Comparison
text:
BEREC
BEREC is intentionally present in both the source corpus and the current-model run. Its preserved BO1A-2024-12-23-55_cat.txt response is also retained. The comparison table above reports its classifications descriptively when a matching current zero-shot output exists.
BEREC is not pooled into the strict aggregate because its Dec. 23 output predates the final Dec. 24 message-role implementation and the precise request state that generated it cannot be established from the surviving files. This avoids turning a provenance uncertainty into an apparent model-generation effect.

title: Model Comparison
text:
Interpretation boundary
A changed binary classification is evidence of model-generation instability under the preserved protocol. It is not, by itself, evidence that the new or legacy classification is more substantively correct. Correctness requires comparison with human coding and, where necessary, examination of the boundary-object evidence and the institutional ambiguities discussed in the manuscript.

title: Six-Scenario Comparison
section: Why the improved protocol is better
text:
Why the improved protocol is better
The improved prompt is intentionally short. It keeps the same documents, 15 questions, zero-shot design, Chat Completions endpoint, and system/user message roles. The substantive treatment is the instruction text; the improved runs also use the same documented 500-token operational output cap.

Evidence boundary: use only the supplied document.
Decision rule: return TRUE only when the document explicitly supports the proposition; otherwise FALSE.
Inference boundary: do not import outside knowledge or infer unstated rules.
Output contract: return exactly one ordered question_id,response row per question.

This makes the coding threshold and serialization contract explicit without adding examples, chain-of-thought instructions, or a structured-output API parameter.

title: Six-Scenario Comparison
text:
Interpretation boundary
Human-reference disagreement is disagreement with the recovered computational reference, not definitive evidence that a model is substantively wrong. Likewise, higher model-generation agreement is stability, not correctness. The design is most informative when both quantities are examined together.
Code

Recovered source corpus
Six boundary objects were recovered and retained as BO1A.txt through BO6A.txt. BO1A.txt is BEREC. The remaining five map to IRG, EU Health Coalition, cOAlition S, CAN, and CEER.

Preserved model outputs
Eleven legacy response files are retained in output/:

one BEREC binary output from Dec. 23, 2024; and
ten Dec. 24, 2024 final-pipeline outputs covering five PONs under zero-shot and step-by-step prompting.

These files are historical artifacts and are not rewritten by the repository’s execution scripts.

Instrument
The legacy computational files contain 15 ordered binary questions. The manuscript later reports 14 prompts; the working-groups question is the additional computational item. The repository keeps all 15 for protocol fidelity.

Human-reference data
The recovered computational evaluation contains one human-reference vector per organization for the five PONs in the final Dec. 24 run. A manuscript-facing three-coder dataset was not recovered from the supplied computational workspace.

BEREC caveat
BEREC was an early development case and is part of the source corpus. Earlier Quarto versions show a different system/user message-role layout during this stage. Because the precise code state that generated BO1A-2024-12-23-55_cat.txt cannot be established with confidence, BEREC’s legacy/current comparison is preserved descriptively but is not pooled into strict same-protocol aggregate statistics.

Current-model extension
The new execution layer asks how a different model behaves under the final 2024 protocol. It does not rerun or replace 2024 outputs. New raw responses and metadata are written only under output/current/, and derived comparisons are written under derived/.
See LEGACY_API_CALLS.md for recovered API-call details and remaining provenance gaps.

title: PON Governance LLM Pilot
text:
This repository contains the computational materials associated with the manuscript Institutional Rules, Boundary Objects, and LLMs — A proof-of-concept for large-N research on the governance of purpose-oriented networks. The manuscript itself is not distributed here.
The project preserves the 2024 LLM outputs as historical evidence and provides a separate execution path for asking a narrowly defined follow-up question:

How does a new model perform under the old protocol?

The comparison changes the model identifier while retaining the final 2024 analytical protocol: the same boundary objects, ordered questions, binary classification task, message structure, and prompting conditions. No structured-output schema, few-shot examples, revised question wording, or other modernized prompting intervention is introduced.

text:
This repository contains the computational materials associated with the manuscript Institutional Rules, Boundary Objects, and LLMs — A proof-of-concept for large-N research on the governance of purpose-oriented networks. The manuscript itself is not distributed here.
The project preserves the 2024 LLM outputs as historical evidence and provides a separate execution path for asking a narrowly defined follow-up question:

How does a new model perform under the old protocol?

The comparison changes the model identifier while retaining the final 2024 analytical protocol: the same boundary objects, ordered questions, binary classification task, message structure, and prompting conditions. No structured-output schema, few-shot examples, revised question wording, or other modernized prompting intervention is introduced.

title: PON Governance LLM Pilot
text:
Corpus
Six purpose-oriented networks are represented in the source corpus:

Body of European Regulators for Electronic Communications (BEREC)
Independent Regulators Group (IRG)
EU Health Coalition
cOAlition S
Climate Action Network (CAN)
Council of European Energy Regulators (CEER)

The recovered final Dec. 24 analysis contains paired zero-shot and step-by-step GPT-4-Turbo outputs for IRG through CEER. A Dec. 23 BEREC binary output is also preserved. Because surviving development reports show that BEREC predates the final message-role layout, its historical comparison is retained but flagged as non-equivalent for strict aggregate statistics.

title: PON Governance LLM Pilot
text:
Reproducibility architecture
The repository deliberately separates three layers:

preserved evidence in output/;
new API executions in timestamped directories under output/current/; and
derived comparisons in derived/.

This separation makes it impossible for the normal new-model workflow to overwrite the 2024 response files.

title: PON Governance LLM Pilot
text:
Reports
Methods documents the corpus, instrument, and recovered API protocol. Legacy Results evaluates the preserved Dec. 24 outputs against the recovered human-reference vectors. Model Comparison becomes the main report after a new-model run is completed and compared with the legacy outputs.
For execution instructions, API-key setup, and provenance cautions, see README.md.

Credential note
One legacy Quarto source contained an API key directly in source code. That credential is intentionally not copied into this repository or this provenance note. If the historical credential has not already been revoked, it should be rotated. The reconstructed project reads credentials only from OPENAI_API_KEY and ignores .env in version control.

title: Methods
text:
The pilot asks whether LLMs can extract governance features from textual boundary objects associated with purpose-oriented networks (PONs). Each document is coded against 15 ordered yes/no governance questions.
The extension uses a zero-shot 3 × 2 design that separates two sources of variation:

Model: GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-5.4 nano, or GPT-5.4 mini.
Protocol: the recovered 2024 prompt or a concise improved prompt.

This yields six scenarios while keeping the five study documents, 15 questions, endpoint, message roles, and binary task fixed.

title: Methods
text:
Zero-shot only
The analytical design no longer uses the historical Let's think step by step condition. Those files remain preserved as archival evidence, but they are excluded from evaluation, plots, tables, and new API runs. Removing that condition makes the comparison easier to interpret: each model/protocol cell differs on one intended dimension rather than mixing model generation with a weakly motivated prompting intervention.

title: Methods
text:
2024 protocol
The final Dec. 24 implementation used Chat Completions with two messages:

a system message containing the policy-analyst instruction and ordered questions;
a user message containing the complete boundary-object text.

The request supplied only model and messages explicitly. No explicit temperature, top-p, token limit, seed, response format, or tools were supplied.
The preserved instruction is:

You are a policy analyst focused on extracting organizational features from documents that regulate the organization and functioning of specific organizations. I will provide the documents and a list of yes-no questions. You will only return TRUE or FALSE responses according to the list of yes-no questions, including a row with the question itself. The output must be in CSV format.

The historical string concatenation, including its whitespace quirks, is retained for all three 2024-protocol cells.

title: Methods
text:
Improved protocol
The improved protocol keeps the same zero-shot task, documents, questions, Chat Completions endpoint, and message roles. The substantive treatment is the instruction text:

Use only the supplied document. For each question, answer TRUE only if the text explicitly supports it; otherwise FALSE. Do not infer unstated rules or use outside knowledge. Return exactly 15 rows as question_id,response, preceded by that header. No other text.

The improvement is deliberately concise. It adds four things the old prompt left underspecified: a source boundary, an explicit TRUE/FALSE decision threshold, a prohibition on unstated inference, and an exact row-level output contract. These changes target both classification ambiguity and the serialization anomalies observed in the contemporary baseline run without introducing examples, chain-of-thought instructions, or a structured-output API parameter. The shorter wording also reduces prompt overhead while leaving the source document and questions unchanged.
All three improved-protocol model arms use the same 500-token maximum output allowance. The client expresses that ceiling with the model-appropriate Chat Completions parameter (max_tokens for GPT-4 Turbo and max_completion_tokens for GPT-5.4 nano and GPT-5.4 mini). The ceiling is an operational execution constraint rather than part of the classification prompt, is held constant across the three improved-protocol arms, and is recorded in the run metadata.
Before execution, the runner uses tiktoken to estimate the two-message request size for every PON. For the GPT-4 Turbo arm, estimated input plus the output cap must remain below 29,750 tokens: the observed 30,000-token account TPM ceiling less a 250-token safety margin. This local preflight was added after the API rejected the largest request at 30,012 requested tokens. Because Chat Completions framing can vary by serving implementation, the local count is treated as a conservative guardrail rather than an exact reconstruction of server-side accounting. A failed preflight creates no batch directory and makes no API call.

title: Methods
text:
BEREC exclusion
BEREC is retained only as archival provenance. Its preserved output predates the final Dec. 24 message-role implementation, and its boundary object is substantially larger than the other study documents. It is excluded from new default runs and from every comparative table, figure, aggregate statistic, and analytical denominator.

title: Methods
text:
Human-reference evaluation
The recovered computational workspace contains one human-reference vector per PON for IRG, EUHC, COAS, CAN, and CEER. All six scenarios are evaluated against these same 75 binary decisions. They should not be conflated with the later three-human-coder validation described in the manuscript.

title: Methods
text:
New-run provenance
Every new request saves the raw model output plus a JSON sidecar containing the requested and returned model IDs, completion ID, UTC request time, prompt and document hashes, usage data, system fingerprint when available, selected response headers, the explicit output-token limit when used, and the parameters deliberately left unspecified. Failed improved-protocol batches receive batch_failed.json; only fully completed batches receive batch_manifest.json. Single-model improved runs receive their own run_manifest.json only after completion.

title: Methods
text:
The computational pilot examines whether a large language model can extract governance features from textual boundary objects associated with purpose-oriented networks (PONs). Each boundary object is presented as a document-level input, and the model returns one binary classification for each governance question.
The contemporary extension implemented in this repository asks a single comparative question: how does a new model perform when the 2024 protocol is held fixed? The model is therefore the intended treatment; the instrument and prompting design are not modernized.

title: Methods
text:
Recovered 2024 API protocol
The final Dec. 24 Quarto implementation used the OpenAI Python client and Chat Completions. The request supplied only model and messages explicitly. The requested model alias was gpt-4-turbo.
The messages were constructed as follows:

System message — the policy-analyst instruction followed by the ordered questions.
User message — the complete boundary-object text.

No explicit values were supplied for temperature, top-p, token limit, seed, structured response format, or tools. Consequently, those values were whatever defaults applied to the service at the time and should not be reconstructed retroactively.
The preserved policy-analyst instruction is:

You are a policy analyst focused on extracting organizational features from documents that regulate the organization and functioning of specific organizations. I will provide the documents and a list of yes-no questions. You will only return TRUE or FALSE responses according to the list of yes-no questions, including a row with the question itself. The output must be in CSV format.

The historical code then concatenated The questions are: and the question list directly to this string. The new runner intentionally preserves that exact string construction rather than cleaning its whitespace.

title: Methods
text:
Prompting conditions
Two conditions are retained:

Zero-shot — the baseline instruction and questions, with no examples.
Step by step — the literal phrase Let's think step by step appended before the question list.

The contemporary runner does not introduce a schema, examples, revised role prompt, or other prompt engineering. Only the requested model ID changes.

title: Methods
text:
BEREC provenance caveat
BEREC was part of the six-PON source corpus and was heavily used while the pipeline was being developed. Its preserved binary output, BO1A-2024-12-23-55_cat.txt, is retained in output/.
That file predates the Dec. 24 final run. Earlier Quarto versions around the BEREC development stage show a different message-role layout, with the boundary-object text used as the system message and the question prompt used as the user message. The surviving materials do not establish with sufficient certainty which exact code state produced the Dec. 23 BEREC file.
Accordingly, current runs include BEREC under the final manuscript-facing protocol, but BEREC is excluded from statistics explicitly labeled as a strict same-protocol legacy comparison. Its legacy/current differences remain available descriptively.

title: Methods
text:
Legacy human-reference evaluation
The recovered Dec. 24 analysis compares each model output with one human-reference vector per organization for IRG, EU Health Coalition, cOAlition S, CAN, and CEER. Those labels are stored in input/reference/legacy_human_responses.csv.
They are the single reference vectors used by the recovered computational code. They should not be conflated with the later three-human-coder validation described in the manuscript.

title: Methods
text:
New-model provenance
Every new request stores the raw model output without normalization, plus a JSON sidecar containing the requested and returned model IDs, completion ID, UTC request time, prompt and input hashes, usage data, system fingerprint when available, selected HTTP headers, and the list of parameters that were deliberately left unspecified.
These additional records improve provenance without altering what is sent to the model.

title: Legacy Results
text:
This report evaluates the ten response files preserved from the Dec. 24, 2024 final pipeline. It does not call OpenAI and does not modify any historical output.
BEREC is not inserted into this human-reference evaluation because its surviving Dec. 23 file comes from an earlier development stage and there is no recovered 15-question BEREC human-reference vector tied unambiguously to that output. BEREC remains part of the source corpus and is handled explicitly in the model-generation comparison.
